cohort: The study included 42,456 deliveries from 2004-2019, focusing on women with liveborn cephalic singleton, term spontaneous labor, and successful planned vaginal birth, comparing those with one previous cesarean birth (LAC group) to nulliparous and parous control groups.
finding: A history of cesarean birth was associated with an increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage even after a successful planned vaginal delivery, with adjusted odds ratios ranging from 2.16 to 2.38.
mod_finding: A history of cesarean birth increased the risk of postpartum hemorrhage following a subsequent successful planned vaginal birth.
